reason: Install the glucose carrier to give the polar fuel a route across the membrane.
expectation: The carrier will form a membrane patch that can transport glucose into the cell, though further steps may be needed.

alternatives.reason: Amino acids should support protein production, but I want to start with glucose transport.

effect: The carrier is installed, so glucose can now be paired with it.
reaction: The placement makes the next transport step clear.
reason: Bring glucose across the membrane to begin following its use as fuel.
expectation: Glucose will enter the cytosol through the carrier, likely moving down its concentration gradient.

alternatives.reason: The pump is needed for the ion-transport goal, but glucose transport is already set up.

effect: Glucose has reached the cytosol, ready for the interior fuel pathway.
reaction: The carrier’s changing shape clearly explains how it transports glucose.
reason: Follow the glucose into the cell interior to begin its breakdown.
expectation: Cytosolic enzymes will begin breaking down glucose, possibly producing an intermediate for aerobic respiration.

alternatives.reason: Oxygen is also needed for aerobic respiration, but I want to follow glucose first.

effect: Glycolysis produced pyruvate and ATP without using oxygen; the pyruvate can now be followed toward mitochondria.
reaction: The distinction between glycolysis and oxygen-dependent steps is clear.
reason: Combine the available oxygen with the glycolytic products to follow aerobic ATP renewal.
expectation: Pyruvate and oxygen will support mitochondrial respiration and further ATP production.

alternatives.reason: Amino acids could advance protein synthesis, but I want to finish following the fuel pathway first.

effect: Aerobic ATP renewal links pyruvate-derived fuel and oxygen to mitochondrial ATP production; the pump still needs installation.
reaction: The separate roles of fuel and oxygen are informative, though the proton gradient is only implied by the arrows.
reason: Install the sodium-potassium pump to prepare for powered ion transport.
expectation: The pump will be embedded in the membrane and become available for an ATP-powered transport step.

alternatives.reason: Placing ATP renewal in the interior may also advance the goal, but the pump needs a membrane first.

effect: The pump is installed and can now be connected to ATP renewal for powered transport.
reaction: The passive-channel inset makes the contrast with the pump useful.
reason: Connect aerobic ATP renewal to the pump to advance the fuel and ion-transport goal.
expectation: ATP will power sodium export and potassium import against their gradients.

alternatives.reason: Protein synthesis also advances a goal, but I want to complete the ATP-to-pump connection first.

effect: Powered transport completes the fuel-to-pump goal; protein synthesis remains.
reaction: The contrast between pumping against gradients and passive flow is clear.
reason: Use the amino acids in the cell interior to advance protein production.
expectation: Ribosomes will use the amino acids to make proteins, perhaps using existing RNA messages.

effect: Protein synthesis completes the remaining goal; the illustration uses existing RNA messages rather than showing their production from DNA.
reaction: The ribosome-to-protein sequence is clear, though GTP's role is not explained.

mostWorthwhile.text: Connecting aerobic ATP renewal to the sodium-potassium pump made the contrast between powered transport and passive flow useful and concrete.

leastWorthwhile.text: Installing the pump was a necessary but predictable setup step, with less to consider than the transport it enabled.

surprise.text: The mitochondrial plan separated fuel oxidation from oxygen's role in electron transfer, while retaining cytosolic ATP production.

arbitrary.text: The offered oxygen combinations with the glucose carrier and pump lacked an obvious purpose in the supplied descriptions; I did not try them.

continue.text: I would continue: the linked transport and energy constructions were informative, although some connections, such as the proton gradient and GTP's role, could use more explanation.
